/-!
# Device law: symmetric Shichman–Hodges square law

Two transistors of a static CMOS inverter, as functions of the gate voltage `u`
(the inverter input) and the drain voltage `v` (the inverter output node).

* NMOS: source at ground (0), gate `u`, drain `v`.
  `In θ u v` is the current from the output node to ground.
* PMOS: source at the supply `θ.VDD`, gate `u`, drain `v`.
  `Ip θ u v` is the current from the supply into the output node.
  `θ.Vtp` is the *magnitude* of the PMOS threshold.

The single expression `(k/2) * (psq (V_GS - V_t) - psq (V_GD - V_t))` equals the
textbook piecewise cutoff / triode / saturation law in forward operation (see
the `*_cutoff`, `*_triode`, `*_sat` lemmas below) and, with source and drain
exchanged, in reverse operation when the output node is outside `[0, VDD]`
(the `*_rev_*` lemmas).

Omitted on purpose: channel-length modulation, body effect, subthreshold
conduction, velocity saturation, junction diodes. See `docs/model.md`.

Units are a convention of the design record (V, µA, fF, ns; `k` in µA/V²);
the mathematics here is unit-free.
-/

import VoltageToBit.Proofs.Existence

/-!
# Gluing trajectories, and existence for a step input

The trajectory notion is pointwise in time: at each instant it relates the
right derivative of the output to the value of the input at that same instant.
Two consequences are recorded here.

* `IsTrajectory.congr_input`: only the input values on `[a, b)` matter.
* `IsTrajectory.concat`: trajectories on `[a, c]` and `[c, b]` that agree at
  `c` glue to a trajectory on `[a, b]`.
* `exists_trajectory_step`: trajectories exist for an input with one jump, of
  the form "`u₁` before `c`, `u₂` from `c` on" with `u₁`, `u₂` continuous.
  This covers the ideal digital edge.

A caution that follows from the same pointwise character. The value the input
takes *at* a jump instant matters: the step above is right-continuous (it takes
the new value at `c`). For an input that keeps its old value at the jump
instant and takes the new value only strictly after it, the right derivative
of any candidate output is dictated by the new value while the inclusion at
that instant refers to the old one. A trajectory that starts in the safe
domain then need not exist on an interval containing the jump, and where none
exists the guarantee says nothing. For the illustrative record, such a step
from 1.8 V to 0 V at `t = 4` and the interval `[0, 10]`, none exists
(`Examples.stepL_no_trajectory` in `Examples/InputClass.lean`). For a general
record, existence is proved only for continuous inputs and for right-continuous
steps.
-/

import VoltageToBit.Proofs.Guarantee

/-!
# What another description of the node must satisfy to be covered

The trajectory notion allows, at each instant, any parameter point of the box
and an additive current error of at most `eps`. This file turns that into the
exact obligation linking the square-law model to any other description of the
same node (a higher-fidelity device model, or the physical device).

* `Design.exists_inBox_of_between`: if a current lies between the net currents
  of two box members (each relaxed by `ε`), then some box member reproduces it
  to within `ε`. The box is convex and the device law is continuous in its
  parameters, so the intermediate value theorem applies along the segment.
* `IsTrajectory.of_model_error`: if on the safe domain the "true" net current
  `J t x` is within `εm` of *some* box member's current, and an additional
  disturbance is bounded by `εw`, with `εm + εw ≤ eps`, then every solution of
  `c * v' = J t (v t) + w t` is a trajectory.
* `IsTrajectory.of_sandwich`: the same with the hypothesis as a sandwich:
  `J t x` lies between the currents of two box members, up to `εm`.
* `IsTrajectory.of_static_sandwich`: the checkable form of the obligation, for
  a model `J x y` that is a function of the input voltage and the node voltage
  only, and an explicit set `U` of input values. The sandwich is required for
  `x ∈ U` and `y` in the safe domain, and the input waveform is required to
  stay in `U`.
* `slew_bound_of_rderiv`: a waveform that is continuous on `[a, b]` and has at
  every instant of `[a, b)` a right derivative of magnitude at most `S` moves
  by at most `S * (t - s)` between two instants `s ≤ t` of `[a, b]`. The
  continuity is needed: a bound on the right derivative alone is not a slew
  bound.
